Sam / Aisha —

Good questions. I analyzed the raw traces from the rw-13b run. Short answers:
- The p95 above 250ms was caused primarily by a handful of long-context requests (average tokens > 400) which trigger KV cache pressure and increased attention kernel time; for the canonical ClinicalNotes_v2 set (avg tokens 42) the p95 for rw-13b is ~220ms. The CSV has both "all_prompts" and "canonical_subset" tabs (see Drive).
- The rw-13b-int8 samples: preliminary human-score delta vs fp16 is -0.03 (mean), SD 0.07 on the 100-sample set provided by Lumina. That's within our acceptable regression threshold (we use 0.05 as hard guardrail) but worth a quick content spot-check on clinical-critical prompts.

Recommendation for pilot rollout:
1) Default to rw-13b-int8 for pilot to hit combined latency/throughput targets; it meets p50/p95 and TTFT targets on canonical set and provides ~15% lower cost per token vs fp16.
2) For high-risk clinical templates (60 prompts flagged in the MAP), route to rw-13b (fp16) with canary 5% traffic and human-in-the-loop QA for two weeks.
3) Add a runtime policy: when avg request tokens > 300, automatically use fp16 variant to avoid tail latency spikes.

Next steps: Neha to update MAP and procurement note with recommended variant and SLA terms; I'll prepare an appendix with the kernel/tracing evidence for your SRE team. Goal: agree on pilot config and PO by 2027-05-03 so we can begin provisioning.
